title: Saleeg (Saliq)
tagline: Creamy Hejazi rice cooked in broth and milk until soft, topped with roasted chicken.
intro: Saleeg is the comforting jewel of Hejazi and Taif cooking — a world away from the spiced kabsa family. Short-grain rice is simmered slowly in chicken broth and milk, stirred until it turns soft, creamy and almost risotto-like, then finished with a whisper of aromatic mastic and crowned with roasted chicken. Mild, soothing and elegant, it is winter and celebration food in the western Kingdom.

items: 4 cardamom pods, 2 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 bay leaves
2–3 pieces mastic (miski), crushed with a little sugar

method: Simmer the chicken with the onion, whole spices and salt until cooked and a good broth forms, about 40 minutes. Lift out the chicken; strain and reserve the broth.

Rinse the rice well. In a heavy pot, bring about 1.2 litres of the broth to a boil, add the rice and simmer, stirring often, until very soft and starting to break down, 25–30 minutes. Add more broth if it thickens too fast.
Stir in the milk, butter and crushed mastic, and keep stirring until creamy and porridge-like. Adjust salt.
Meanwhile roast or grill the chicken until golden.
Spread the creamy rice on a platter, top with the roasted chicken and a little melted butter. Serve with daqoos.
tips: Use a starchy short/medium-grain rice, not basmati — the creaminess is the whole point.
Stir often, like a risotto, to release the starch and prevent sticking.
Mastic (miski) gives saleeg its distinctive gentle aroma — a little goes a long way.
toServe: Serve piping hot with sharp, spicy daqoos to cut the richness.
imageAlt: Saleeg creamy Hejazi rice topped with roasted chicken
